ab-experiment.what: Designs an A/B test with a hypothesis, sample size and decision rules, then analyses the results against that plan
ab-experiment.when: you need to know whether an experiment worked and how long it must run

accessibility.what: Audits screens against WCAG 2.2 AA, fixes what it can at the source and leaves a regression gate in CI
accessibility.when: keyboard, screen-reader or low-vision users may not be able to finish a flow

adr.what: Records a decision already made as a numbered ADR with its context, the options weighed and its consequences
adr.when: a choice has been made and future readers will ask why

analytics-events.what: Designs the analytics event sheet, wires events through one typed module and audits the code against the sheet
analytics-events.when: you are tracking a feature, or the numbers in the dashboard look wrong

android.what: Applies the Android house rules to Kotlin and Compose code and reviews diffs against its checklist, gated by make check
android.when: you write, change or review Kotlin or Java code in an Android app

api-versioning.what: Deprecates and retires API endpoints with Sunset headers, a breaking-change diff and a removal gate read from the logs
api-versioning.when: an endpoint has to change or go away without stranding its consumers

app-store-release.what: Prepares an App Store or Google Play submission in a release doc and prints the upload commands for you to run
app-store-release.when: a mobile build is going to TestFlight or the stores, or review rejected it

architecture-diagram.what: Draws C4 and sequence diagrams from the code as it is, with a source for every box and a list of what is unconfirmed
architecture-diagram.when: you need a picture of the system that matches the code, not the README

auth.what: Builds authentication and authorisation for a service, with a permission matrix that runs as one test per cell
auth.when: you are adding login or roles, or need to know who can read whose data

autopilot.what: Runs unattended from one requirement statement to a prepared merge request, recording each decision as Proposed
autopilot.when: you want a requirement built end to end without answering questions on the way

background-jobs.what: Builds queue, cron or outbox jobs that are safe to run twice, with bounded retries, dead letters and a runbook stub
background-jobs.when: work runs outside the request and must survive retries, crashes and duplicates

backlog.what: Turns PRD statements into epics and Given-When-Then stories, with a coverage matrix that a script checks
backlog.when: a PRD is ready and the team needs stories it can plan, build and test

branch-review.what: Reviews a branch, patch or path, has each Critical and High finding verified independently, and gives a merge verdict
branch-review.when: a change needs a second pair of eyes before it is merged

ci-pipeline.what: Generates or refreshes the GitLab CI or GitHub Actions pipeline for the stack, with every job calling a make target
ci-pipeline.when: a repository has no pipeline, or its pipeline has drifted from the template

client-deliverables.what: Builds the numbered client documentation pack, each document as Markdown and versioned Word, with a delivery checklist
client-deliverables.when: a client is due a documentation delivery and expects Word documents

client-handover.what: Writes the end-of-engagement handover pack, every line sourced from the repository or marked unconfirmed
client-handover.when: an engagement is ending and the client's next team must run the system

cloud-cost.what: Reviews a month of the cloud bill read-only, works out cost per request and proposes cuts as commands to run
cloud-cost.when: the cloud bill has grown and you need to know where the money goes

company-attribution.what: Sets who owns a repository through a company profile, then fills LICENSE, CODEOWNERS and package metadata from it
company-attribution.when: a repository needs a licence, an owner or the right company name on it

computer-vision.what: Builds an image feature with group-based splits, a baseline to beat and a threshold set from the cost of errors
computer-vision.when: you need to classify images, spot defects or read fields from scanned documents

data-model.what: Designs the data model from the stories, giving every column a reason, with a runnable schema.sql that a gate checks
data-model.when: stories are agreed and you need to know which tables and columns to build

data-pipeline.what: Applies the data stack rules to dbt models and Airflow 3 DAGs: idempotent partitions, tested marts, safe backfills
data-pipeline.when: you write or change dbt models or Airflow DAGs, or plan a warehouse backfill

database.what: Applies its rules for schemas, indexes, slow queries and store choice on PostgreSQL, ClickHouse and MongoDB
database.when: a query is slow, an index is in doubt, or a feature needs a place to store data

dataset-generation.what: Grows at least 10 real rows into deduplicated, contamination-checked eval or training data, with a datasheet
dataset-generation.when: you have a few real examples and need many more for an eval or a training run

db-migration.what: Writes a database migration with a tested Down step, lock-safety notes and the deploy order against the code
db-migration.when: you are changing a schema that live traffic and the previous release still use

definition-of-done.what: Checks a branch against the Definition of Done item by item, with a command or a file line as evidence for each
definition-of-done.when: you think a task is finished and want proof before the merge request

dependency-audit.what: Audits dependencies for vulnerabilities and outdated versions, then applies only the upgrades you approve, each gated
dependency-audit.when: packages are out of date, or an advisory names one you ship

deployment-architecture.what: Documents what runs where in each environment, with a diagram and a source or unconfirmed mark on every claim
deployment-architecture.when: someone on call needs to know how the system is deployed and rolled back

design-critique.what: Scores a UI design against its flows and design system with measured contrast and screenshots, worst finding first
design-critique.when: a design or prototype is about to go to the client or into handoff

design-directions.what: Produces visual directions over the real screens, one impeccable pick or three distinct variants, and records the choice
design-directions.when: the screens exist but nobody has chosen how the product should look

design-system.what: Turns a chosen design direction into oklch tokens, per-stack themes and a lint that keeps new colour literals out
design-system.when: a look has been agreed and the code should be held to it

docs-drift.what: Finds docs that no longer match the code and fixes the stale side, or reports code that has left its design
docs-drift.when: you inherit a codebase or suspect the README no longer tells the truth

doctor.what: Checks this machine and repository are set up for Bearing and gives a fix you can type for each real miss
doctor.when: a hook did not fire or you are not sure the kit is installed properly

estimate.what: Sizes the remaining backlog in points and hours and answers the date question with a margin from measured velocity
estimate.when: someone asks how long the backlog will take or whether go-live still holds

explain-codebase.what: Explains how a repository or feature works, read-only, with a path and line number behind every claim
explain-codebase.when: you are new to the code or need to find where something is handled

feature-flags.what: Adds, uses or removes a feature flag through one typed module, with an owner, a removal date and tests for both states
feature-flags.when: a change must merge dark, or an old flag is ready to come out

feature-patterns.what: Plans one common mechanism, such as uploads, search or payments, as a design doc before any code is written
feature-patterns.when: a feature needs a well-known mechanism that is easy to get wrong the first time

flutter.what: Holds Dart code to the Flutter house rules for Riverpod state, repositories and loading states, and reviews Dart diffs
flutter.when: you write, review or scaffold a Flutter app in Dart

gate-audit.what: Audits every CI job, hook and make check for gates that pass on empty input or check nothing, and names the fix
gate-audit.when: you suspect a green check is not actually checking anything

genai-design.what: Writes a solution document for a GenAI feature that names one metric, one approach and the cheaper option it rejected
genai-design.when: you are deciding how to build a feature with an LLM, before any code exists

git-hooks.what: Installs or repairs the committed git hooks, sets core.hooksPath and proves each hook on failing and passing input
git-hooks.when: a clone runs no hooks, or a commit was rejected and you need to know why

go.what: Applies the Go house rules for net/http, pgx, sqlc and goose, and reviews Go diffs for tenant scope and race traps
go.when: you write, change or review Go code, or start a new Go service

harness-setup.what: Sets up a repository for another coding agent such as Cursor or Codex, carrying its rules, hooks and denies across
harness-setup.when: part of the team works in a coding agent other than Claude Code

health-checks.what: Builds /healthz and /readyz endpoints with per-dependency checks, plus probes, alerts or synthetic journeys when asked
health-checks.when: a service needs liveness and readiness, or an outage should page someone

high-level-design.what: Writes a High Level Design once its goal is agreed, then has an independent critic grade it before approval
high-level-design.when: a new system or large feature needs a design that reviewers can challenge

i18n.what: Moves user-facing strings into per-platform catalogs with plurals, locale formats and RTL, gated by a missing-key check
i18n.when: the app needs another language or has to work right to left

incident.what: Keeps the live incident record as scribe, with severity, a UTC timeline and comms, while people run every fix
incident.when: something is down in production and the response needs a record and a plan

infra.what: Applies the infrastructure rules to Terraform and Kubernetes changes, where CI posts the plan and a person applies it
infra.when: you change or review Terraform, kustomize overlays or alert rules

ios.what: Applies the iOS house rules for Swift 6, SwiftUI and strict concurrency, and reviews Swift diffs against its checklist
ios.when: you write, change or review Swift code for an iPhone app

learn.what: Lists, adds and proposes the learnings Bearing keeps on this machine, and only with your consent
learn.when: you want Bearing to remember a lesson or share recurring ones upstream

license-compliance.what: Checks third-party licences against an allow and deny policy and writes the SBOM or notices a release needs
license-compliance.when: you must know whether you may ship what you depend on, and what you owe

llm-agent.what: Builds an LLM agent on the Anthropic SDK whose tools carry permission tiers and whose loop has turn and cost limits
llm-agent.when: you want a model to take actions through tools, alone or as several agents

llm-eval.what: Turns an LLM feature's success metric into a person-labelled golden set, graders and a CI gate that fails on regression
llm-eval.when: you need to know whether a prompt or model change made a feature better or worse

llm-fine-tuning.what: Plans and smoke-tests fine-tuning of an open model once evals show prompting and RAG fall short, then serves it on vLLM
llm-fine-tuning.when: prompting, retrieval and a larger model still miss the target on your eval

llm-gateway.what: Finds every model call in the code and moves it behind one gateway module with routing, retries, cost and kill switches
llm-gateway.when: model calls are scattered through the code or you cannot see what they cost

llm-guardrails.what: Adds input, tool-call and output checks around an LLM feature from a reviewable policy, proven by adversarial tests
llm-guardrails.when: an LLM feature takes untrusted text, handles personal data or acts through tools

load-test.what: Writes k6 load tests from the SLOs with failing thresholds and a manual CI job, and refuses production hosts
load-test.when: you need to know whether a service meets its SLO at peak traffic

logging.what: Sets up one structured logger that carries the request id across async hops and keeps personal data out of the logs
logging.when: your logs leak personal data or cannot be joined to the request that wrote them

low-level-design.what: Writes a low level design for one HLD component, down to files, types, indexed queries, named tests and MR-sized work
low-level-design.when: an agreed HLD component needs a detailed plan before anyone writes code

mcp-server.what: Builds an MCP server or client in Python or TypeScript, with tiered tools, both transports and a protocol test per tool
mcp-server.when: you want models to reach an API or service of yours as MCP tools

merge-request.what: Runs the gate, audits the commits and drafts the merge request description for the current branch, never pushing it
merge-request.when: a branch is finished and you want the MR text and the push command ready

model-routing.what: Measures candidate models on a feature's eval and writes the cheapest route or cascade that still clears the threshold
model-routing.when: you want to cut LLM spend without dropping below a feature's quality bar

motion-design.what: Builds a requested animation from the motion tokens with a reduced-motion path, then checks it with the motion gate
motion-design.when: a screen needs animation that stays smooth and respects people who asked for less motion

new-repo.what: Creates a new repository shaped like its siblings, with Makefile, CI, hooks, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, then runs its gate
new-repo.when: you are starting a new service or app that should match the repositories beside it

new-skill.what: Writes a new Bearing skill in the kit's house format, validates it and evals it against a baseline run without the skill
new-skill.when: a repeated checklist or job should become a skill other engineers can trigger

nextjs.what: Applies the Next.js App Router rules on server components, authorised server actions and caching, and reviews diffs
nextjs.when: you build or review pages, routes or server actions in a Next.js app

node.what: Applies the Node backend rules for Fastify 5, Zod, Drizzle and pino, and reviews TypeScript server diffs
node.when: you write or review a TypeScript backend service running on Node

observability.what: Wires OpenTelemetry so one trace id joins logs, spans and metrics, then adds RED dashboards and SLO burn-rate alerts
observability.when: you cannot tell from production signals whether a service works or why it is slow

on-call.what: Writes the on-call rotation, escalation and error budget policy, and checks that every paging alert has a runbook
on-call.when: you need to decide who gets paged, how a page escalates and what a burnt budget costs

onboard-repo.what: Brings an existing repository onto the standard within its own conventions, with a make check that mirrors CI
onboard-repo.when: you inherit or adopt a repository that predates the standard files

openapi-spec.what: Designs or audits the OpenAPI 3.1 contract in api/openapi.yaml, writes readable API docs and counts drift from the code
openapi-spec.when: an API needs a written contract, or the spec and the code may have drifted apart

performance.what: Profiles a slow path at production size, fixes the cause one change at a time and reports before and after numbers
performance.when: something is too slow or uses too much memory and you need a measured fix

postmortem.what: Writes a blameless postmortem from incident notes, with impact in numbers, a UTC timeline and a root cause chain
postmortem.when: an incident is over and the team needs a written account it can learn from

prd.what: Turns a brief, notes or a ticket into a PRD of numbered, testable REQ statements and a register of open questions
prd.when: you have a brief or client notes and need requirements that everything can trace back to

privacy-review.what: Maps personal data against what was promised, traces each retention and deletion path end to end and fixes the breaks
privacy-review.when: you must show that delete really deletes and retention matches the published promise

prompt-registry.what: Moves prompts into a versioned registry loaded by one module, with typed variables, render tests and a score per version
prompt-registry.when: you are writing, improving or auditing the prompts a product sends to a model

prose-lint.what: Finds em dashes, AI filler and self-praise in prose people read and rewrites whole sentences, checking each claim
prose-lint.when: docs, MR text or UI copy read as machine-written or may promise more than the code does

python.what: Applies the Python house rules for FastAPI, Pydantic v2, async SQLAlchemy and Alembic, and reviews Python diffs
python.when: you write, change or review Python code, from an API service to a command-line tool

rag.what: Builds retrieval-augmented generation on pgvector whose answers cite sources, measured by recall and MRR on a golden set
rag.when: answers must come from your own documents and show where each claim came from

react.what: Applies the React house rules for TanStack Query, Zustand and Zod at every boundary, and reviews TSX diffs
react.when: you write or review components and hooks in a React app built with Vite

react-native.what: Applies the React Native house rules for Expo, expo-router and secure token storage, and reviews mobile diffs
react-native.when: you build or review screens in an Expo app that ships to iOS and Android

refactor.what: Restructures code without changing behaviour, one mechanical transform per commit, tests green before and after each
refactor.when: code needs reshaping, renaming or splitting and nothing a test can see may change

release.what: Works out the next version from the commits or the API diff, writes the CHANGELOG section and prints the tag commands
release.when: a service or package is ready to version and you want the changelog and tag commands

resilience-testing.what: Turns the design's failure claims into fault plans and restore drills, first predicting from the code which will fail
resilience-testing.when: you need to know whether the system survives a dead dependency or a lost database

runbook.what: Writes or updates the runbook for one alert, with diagnosis commands, remediation, rollback and escalation
runbook.when: an alert can fire and whoever is paged needs to know what to check and do

screen-design.what: Designs every screen in every state, desktop and phone, as clickable React or HTML mockups before any product code
screen-design.when: the flows are agreed and a reviewer needs screens to click through and approve

secrets.what: Inventories and scans secrets by name without seeing a value, and prints the rotation and leak response steps to run
secrets.when: a key was committed, a secret needs rotating or nobody knows which secrets exist

session-handoff.what: Writes a handoff note for the next session on this branch: where work stopped, what is local only, what to do first
session-handoff.when: you are pausing, clearing context or handing the branch to someone else

simplify-code.what: Deletes code a change does not need, such as dead code and one-use abstractions, with the tests green after each cut
simplify-code.when: a change, often AI-written, carries more code than the job needs

speech.what: Builds transcription, text-to-speech or a real-time voice agent, measured by WER per language and latency per stage
speech.when: you need to transcribe calls, speak replies aloud or run a voice agent

spike.what: Answers one yes, no or number question inside a timebox using throwaway code, leaving only a written recommendation
spike.when: a decision depends on something nobody knows yet and you want a bounded answer

start-task.what: Cuts a ticket's branch from the base it will ship from, runs a baseline and checks the criteria against the repository
start-task.when: you are picking up a ticket and want to start on the right branch

tabular-ml.what: Builds a classical model on tables or events with a leak-checked split, a baseline it must beat and drift monitoring
tabular-ml.when: you need to predict churn, score accounts, forecast demand or flag anomalies

task-report.what: Writes the end-of-task report under Changed, Verified, Not done and Noticed, every line backed by a command or a file
task-report.when: work is finished and someone who was not there needs a true account of it

tech-debt.what: Keeps the tech debt register in docs/DEBT.md, seeded from TODOs, suppressions and skipped tests, ranked by weekly cost
tech-debt.when: you want to choose what to clean up next by cost rather than by who complains

tech-decision.what: Lays out the options for a technology choice, recommends one with reasons, lets you decide and records it as an ADR
tech-decision.when: you must choose between technologies, such as two message brokers or two clouds

test-automation.what: Sets up or extends the stack's own automated test suite and writes one test per planned test case, named by its TC id
test-automation.when: planned test cases need to become automated tests in the stack's own framework

test-cases.what: Turns acceptance criteria into a risk register, TC-numbered test cases and a test plan, with no test code
test-cases.when: QA needs test cases and a plan derived from the acceptance criteria

test-heal.what: Classifies each failing or flaky test with evidence, heals locator, timing and data drift, and leaves regressions red
test-heal.when: tests fail or flake and you need to know which are drift and which are real bugs

test-run.what: Runs every test suite the repository has into one report, naming each failure at file:line and each suite not run
test-run.when: you want to know what is failing and which tests actually ran

themes.what: Adds or checks themes such as dark mode or a tenant brand, keeping the current mode intact and proving contrast
themes.when: the product needs dark mode, a high contrast theme or a brand per tenant

threat-model.what: Writes a STRIDE threat model before code, tying assets, boundaries and entry points to rated threats and mitigations
threat-model.when: a feature touches auth, payments, personal data or outside input and needs defences planned

traceability.what: Builds the traceability matrix from requirements to stories, tests and commits, and counts every broken link it finds
traceability.when: you need to know whether every requirement is tested and delivered before sign-off

tracker-sync.what: Creates and updates tickets in the configured tracker, syncs the backlog and moves status only when the rules are met
tracker-sync.when: backlog items need tickets, or a ticket's status and MR link need updating

upgrade-tools.what: Upgrades the Claude Code plugins and skill packs on this machine after reviewing each diff, noting each version change
upgrade-tools.when: your plugins or skill packs are behind and you want them updated with care

ux-flows.what: Maps a feature's screens, states and copy against its stories, with flow diagrams and a gate that fails on any dead end
ux-flows.when: you need to know which screens a feature needs and what users see when it fails

vapt-report.what: Writes the VAPT report for a release from triaged scanner findings and the threat model, ending in a ship or block call
vapt-report.when: a release needs a written security position before it ships

verify-deploy.what: Checks readiness, health, version and smoke pages on one environment after you deploy, read-only and never rolling back
verify-deploy.when: you have just deployed and want evidence that the right version is up

webhooks.what: Builds inbound webhooks that verify signatures and process each event once, and outbound ones with retries and a log
webhooks.when: you are receiving or sending webhooks and need them trustworthy and traceable

workflow.what: Reads where the work stands from the repository, branch and diff, and names the skill or step that comes next
workflow.when: you are unsure what to do next, which skill fits or what the team has in flight
